summary: The range improves machine-B reproducibility, but two newly scripted headline quantities still encode known denominator problems: missing ages enter the age-8+ population, and HLINK “match rates” count pairs rather than distinct linked people. The most important fix is to define and assert the eligible person-level denominator and numerator before publishing the scripted rates; the runner also needs an actual checksum comparison for the mortality table before claiming five byte-identical reproductions.

findings.title: The newly scripted age-8+ denominators retain records with missing age
findings.what_the_code_does: Both scripts execute `keep if age >= 8`, then immediately record `_N` through `repnum`. In Stata, numeric missing values exceed 8, so these counts include every record with `age==.`; the registry nevertheless describes them as people “aged 8 and above.”
findings.why_it_matters: If either source contains missing ages, the published denominators 57,589,273 and 115,030,746 are too large for the stated population, and every linkage rate using them is understated. The restricted denominators inherit the same contamination through `cn1940_full`.
findings.how_to_check: On machine B, run `count if missing(age)` immediately after each `use names1940, clear`, and separately tabulate `count if age>=8` versus `count if age>=8 & !missing(age)`; repeat after merging the discordant flag.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `keep if age >= 8 & !missing(age)` in both scripts, regenerate all four denominators and dependent rates, and update the draft and claim registry to the corrected values.

findings.title: The scripted HLINK rates divide matched-pair rows by a person denominator without establishing one pair per person
findings.what_the_code_does: `prep_links` removes only duplicate `(histid1930,histid1940)` pairs via `duplicates drop histid1930 histid1940, force`. The new statistic then computes `100*_N/N_men_1940_full` after restricting pairs to eligible 1940 IDs. It does not reduce to one observation per `histid1940` or assert that `histid1940` is unique.
findings.why_it_matters: The reported 58.06% and 59.52% are pairs per eligible person, not necessarily the share of eligible people linked. Any 1940 person appearing in multiple pairs inflates the numerator and can distort both levels and the before/after change.
findings.how_to_check: Immediately after the merge at line 291, run `isid histid1940`; if it fails, run `duplicates report histid1940` and compare the current `_N` rate with `egen tag=tag(histid1940)` followed by `count if tag`.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the estimand explicitly. For a person linkage rate, count distinct eligible `histid1940` values and assert the intended uniqueness constraints; if pairs per person is intentional, relabel the statistic and draft language accordingly.

findings.title: The runner cannot substantiate its claim that all five tables reproduced byte-identically
findings.what_the_code_does: The documentation claims that five tables, including mortality, were SHA-256 identical. The comparison script's `TABLES` list contains only `abe_jw`, `abe_jw_restricted`, `hlink`, and `hlink_restricted`; it never compares `linkage_table_mortality_bunmd.tex`. Moreover, `read()` normalizes CRLF to LF before comparison, so its four comparisons are text-equivalence checks rather than SHA-256 byte comparisons.
findings.why_it_matters: A successful `Run-MachineB.ps1` does not verify the mortality output at all and does not perform the advertised byte-level test. The central replication claim therefore lacks reproducible evidence in the committed workflow.
findings.how_to_check: Run `rg -n "mortality|sha|hash" replication/extract_deaglan_tables.py replication/Run-MachineB.ps1`; then independently run `Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256` on the regenerated and committed copies of all five table files and compare the hashes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the mortality filename to a dedicated five-file comparison step, compare raw bytes or explicit SHA-256 hashes, print and retain both hashes in the run log or manifest, and reserve normalized-text comparison for the separate tabular-extraction task.

verified_clean.item: The code/data path split was applied consistently to the scripts changed in this range.
verified_clean.evidence: Modified LINKAGE entry points set `$LCODE` and load `$LCODE/shared/paths.do`; `LINKAGE/code/shared/paths.do:30-46` validates the code root and derives code globals from it while leaving data under `$ROOT`.

verified_clean.item: The machine-B preflight covers the direct code and data inputs read by the three table scripts.
verified_clean.evidence: `replication/run_machineB.do:44-68` enumerates the ABE/JW, HLINK, truth, flag, and mortality inputs corresponding to the direct `use`/`import` statements in the invoked table scripts.

verified_clean.item: The new HLINK diagnostic calculation does not leak its merge state into subsequent table construction.
verified_clean.evidence: The added block is balanced by `preserve` and `restore` at `LINKAGE/code/02_hlink/linkage_analysis_newlinks.do:289-294`.

verified_clean.item: The claim registry is syntactically valid and its new result keys trace to explicit producers.
verified_clean.evidence: `replication/claims.toml` parsed successfully with Python `tomllib`; keys at lines 489, 497, 505, 513, and 521 correspond to `repnum` calls in the two linkage-analysis scripts.

verified_clean.item: The four-table extraction fails visibly on a missing or textually different regenerated linkage table.
verified_clean.evidence: `replication/extract_deaglan_tables.py:92-104` sets `failed=True` for missing or differing files, and line 119 returns a nonzero exit status.

verified_clean.item: No new causal estimation or treatment-effect specification was introduced in the reviewed range.
verified_clean.evidence: The analytical additions in `LINKAGE/code/01_abe_jw/linkage_analysis.do:21-25` and `LINKAGE/code/02_hlink/linkage_analysis_newlinks.do:26-30,282-295` expose denominators and rates from frozen link files; they do not add regressions or identification assumptions.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so claims-vs-code could only assess claims embedded in repository documentation and `replication/claims.toml`; prose claims in the paper were not reviewed.
The external datasets on machine B were not available in this workspace, so the number of missing-age records and duplicate HLINK person IDs could not be measured.
The Stata pipeline and four-hour machine-B runner could not be executed here; runtime conclusions are source-based except for the committed outputs and documentation.

The historical linkage files are frozen outputs, and the range does not reproduce the underlying HLINK matching or fully reproduce ABE/JW matching. Selection into linkage and circularity between transcription quality and linkability therefore remain untestable from this run.
